cards.text: Absalom, King David's son, fled to Geshur and has stayed there three years. Now David's heart longs for Absalom. And Joab son of Zeruiah, commander of David's army, can see it.

cards.question: Joab comes up with a plan. He sends to the town of Tekoa to bring back a ___ woman.

cards.text: Joab wants her to pretend to be a mourner. Friend, the man isn't hiring a messenger, he's CASTING A ROLE.

cards.question: To play the part, Joab tells the woman from Tekoa to wear her finest clothes and anoint herself with oil.
Joab sends the woman from Tekoa to the king with something to say. Whose words is she bringing?

cards.text: Costume on, lines ready, SHOWTIME. She goes in to the king and falls facedown in homage.

cards.question: The woman from Tekoa's first words to King David are a cry for help.

cards.text: David asks her, "What troubles you?" And here comes Joab's script: she's a widow, and her husband is dead.

cards.question: The widow tells David she had two sons who got into a fight out in the field. How does the fight end?

answers.text: One struck the other and killed him
One drove the other out of the land
One took the other's whole inheritance

cards.question: The widow says someone in the field stepped in to separate her two sons.

cards.text: Now the whole clan has risen up against her, and they want the son who's left. That's not a family meeting, friend, that's an AMBUSH.

cards.question: The clan wants the widow to hand over her last son. What do they plan to do with him?

answers.text: Put him to death for his brother's life
Send him away from the land for good
Make him a servant to the whole clan

cards.text: She calls that last son "my one remaining ember". Friend, I live next to ovens, and I KNOW what happens when the last ember goes out.

cards.question: The clan says they'll cut off the heir too. If they do, the widow says her husband's ___ won't be preserved on the earth.

cards.text: I think David's moved. "Go home," he tells her, "and I will give orders on your behalf."

cards.question: The woman from Tekoa tells David that if there's any blame in this, it should fall on the king and his throne.

cards.text: David says if anyone says a word to her, bring him to the king. But she wants more: she asks David to invoke the LORD to keep the avenger of blood away from her son.

cards.question: The woman from Tekoa asks David to invoke the LORD to protect her son. What does David vow?

answers.text: Not a hair of his head will fall
The avenger will be put to death
The whole clan will be banished

cards.text: Now she's got the king's vow, sworn by the LORD. Then she asks, "Please, may your servant speak a word to my lord the king?" and David tells her to go ahead.

cards.question: Then the woman from Tekoa turns the whole thing around on David. What does she say his own ruling convicts him of?

answers.text: Not bringing back his own banished son
Ignoring the widows of his kingdom
Breaking an old vow to the LORD

cards.text: I bet David didn't even know he was on trial. Then she says we will surely die and be like water poured out on the ground, and that water can't be recovered.

cards.question: The woman tells David that God devises ways that the banished one may not be cast out from Him.

cards.text: Then she says the people have made her afraid. So she came to the king, hoping he would deliver her and her son.

cards.question: Remember, the clan wanted to cut off the heir. Now the woman says a man would cut off both her and her son from God's ___.

cards.text: And then she lays it on THICK: the king can discern good and evil, just like the angel of God. Friend, the nicest thing anybody ever said about me was "this one still works."

cards.question: David tells the woman, "I am going to ask you something; do not conceal it from me!" Whose hand does he ask is behind all this?
When David asks, the woman from Tekoa denies that anyone told her what to say.

cards.text: She says Joab did all this to bring about a change of affairs, and then she STILL squeezes in one more compliment about the king's wisdom. Caught red-handed, and she's still working the room.

cards.question: Now David turns to Joab himself. What does the king tell him to do?

answers.text: Go and send the woman home
Go and punish Absalom in Geshur

cards.text: Joab falls facedown and blesses the king. He says today he knows he's found favor in the king's eyes.

cards.question: So Joab gets up, goes to Geshur and brings Absalom to ___.

cards.text: Absalom's back, but hold on, friend, because the king adds a condition.

cards.question: Absalom is back from Geshur. What is King David's condition for him?

answers.text: He must not see the king's face
He must stay outside the city walls
He must never speak to Joab again

cards.text: Not a man in all Israel is as handsome and highly praised as Absalom, without a single flaw from the sole of his foot to the top of his head. Meanwhile I got a little soft around the edges and ended up in a DRAWER.

cards.question: And then there's Absalom's hair. Once a year he shaves it off. Why?

answers.text: He made a vow to the LORD

cards.text: When he cuts it, he weighs it: two hundred shekels, by the royal standard. Friend, the man doesn't get a haircut, he gets a WEIGH-IN.
Absalom has three sons, and a daughter who is a beautiful woman.

cards.question: Absalom's daughter is named ___.

cards.text: Absalom lives in Jerusalem two years without seeing the king's face. TWO YEARS, friend, and believe me, I get it, because I spent years in a drawer in the same kitchen as the oven.

cards.question: Absalom sends for Joab so Joab can send him to the king. What does Joab do?
Absalom sends for Joab a second time, and this time Joab comes.

cards.text: Absalom's done waiting. Joab's field is right next to his, and it's got barley in it.

cards.question: What does Absalom tell his servants to do to Joab's barley field?

cards.text: Two invitations ignored, but one fire and NOW Joab shows up. He comes to Absalom's house demanding, "Why did your servants set my field on fire?"

cards.question: Absalom tells Joab it would be better for him if he were still in ___.
Absalom asks to see the king's face and says that if there is iniquity in him, let the king kill him.

cards.text: So Joab goes and tells the king, and David summons Absalom. Absalom comes and bows facedown before him.

cards.question: Absalom is facedown before his father, King David. What does the king do?

answers.text: He sends him back to Geshur
He orders him out of the city

cards.text: A kiss, after all that. Keep your apron on, friend, because this story still has a long way to go.

findings.problem: Stop 3, card 11 quotes "this one still works.", which isn't the exact BSB wording.

rule.text: Quotes: Quotation marks around Bible words mean the exact BSB wording, punctuation included.

findings.problem: The card introduces Absalom as King David's son, but none of its cited verses supports that relationship. The outside fact needs its own supporting reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: Cards 1-5 go item by item through the descriptive aside in 2 Samuel 14:25-27: Absalom's appearance, his annual haircut and its weight, and his children. This stretch should be summed up in one story card, without choice cards, rather than expanded into three story cards and two choice cards.

rule.text: If a stretch is mostly detail and not much happens, it counts. The rule: Papa Dorin sums up the stretch in one story card. He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item. A long stretch never gets a choice card.
